step: Selection fix across text/images/shapes (EDT-13..18 UX, not a new feature ID). Owner's live-use recipe showed a shape left invisibly selected get swept into a move_objects with four words that were never meant to move together. Root cause: four separate selections (arrange.ts shared + overlay.ts/images.ts/shapes.ts each their own) kept in sync only by convention. Fixed centrally: viewer.ts's new deselectAll() + arrange.ts's new onSelectOnly/onActivate callbacks. A plain click on any object now clears the other kinds' tool-level highlight (root cause of the first test failure: overlay.ts's clearSelection() used to call inspector.showEmpty() unconditionally, clobbering a shape/image panel just shown moments earlier in the same click -- fixed by never touching the inspector there; every caller that wants the empty state calls showEmpty() itself now). Esc, or a plain click on empty page/the grey area around it, deselects everything, asking first with an unapplied text draft. Ctrl/Cmd+click joins Shift+click; a plain click on one member of a multi-selection narrows to it. After move/nudge/align/duplicate/paste the object stays selected AND visibly highlighted now (new shapeTool.selectIndex/imageTool.selectIndex follow a new arrange.sole() after every redraw -- arrange.ts's own re-find-by-rectangle alone missed any move made through the shape/image's own box, since only arrange.ts's own moveSelection/align update pageRect, so it now also matches by the object's stable index). A text Apply/Enter, Delete, undo/redo and a command-bar edit all clear the selection instead of reselecting (owner: 'selection remains even after application and confuses the user'). Images/shapes' own separate Delete/Escape keydown listener is gone (was a double-Op risk on Delete); one shared path now. 16 Playwright tests rewritten/added.

openQuestions.text: SIG-02/03: only PAdES level B-B by default, B-T with an RFC 3161 timestamp -- not B-LT/LTA, which need embedded OCSP/CRL revocation info a locally generated self-signed certificate has no real source for. Deliberate scope limit, not an oversight.

FRM-04: a text-field blank made of underscore *characters* (not a drawn line) is never detected -- the same text-overlap guard that suppresses false positives on ordinary paragraph text can't distinguish "this text IS the field cue" from "this text is prose". On a 180-degree-rotated page, the left/right/above label-search heuristics assume an unrotated layout, so a real field may be detected with no label attached (lower confidence, never the wrong label, never a phantom).

FRM-07: CSV export doesn't sanitize field *names* against spreadsheet formula injection (a field literally named "=cmd|..." exports with a leading-= cell) -- the usual defusing-prefix mitigation isn't reliably invertible without breaking FRM-07's own round-trip guarantee, so this is documented rather than fixed. XFDF loses a bare \r from \r\n line endings in a multiline value on round-trip -- inherent XML line-ending normalization (every compliant parser does this), not a bug in this codebase.

SEC-08: partial redaction of a curve or multi-segment path removes it in full rather than clipping -- only a single straight line or an axis-aligned rectangle get real sub-rectangle/segment clipping. General polygon clipping was out of scope for the first pass.

SEC-11: redaction verification re-extracts text/images/vectors and checks the raw content stream, but can't see a fully orphaned XObject that's present in /Resources but never invoked by a Do operator -- not visually recoverable by any renderer, but a raw object-stream reader could still find its bytes. Documented in verify_redaction's docstring as out of scope.

FRM-02: a form field needing a character outside Helvetica/Times/Courier/ZapfDingbats (e.g. an emoji, a currency symbol the field's current font lacks) is refused rather than filled -- confirmed by reading PyMuPDF's installed source that Widget.update() hard-locks the appearance font to one of those 4 base-14 faces, so there is no API path to attach a Unicode-coverage font to an AcroForm text field's appearance.

FRM-06: single-page flatten pastes a captured pixmap (not PyMuPDF's own document-wide bake()), since 1.28.2 has no page-scoped bake. Measured ~0.2-0.3% pixel diff vs a full bake (antialiasing residue, not missing content) -- fine for now, revisit if PyMuPDF adds page-scoped flattening.

FNT-20 protects icons/emoji from being redrawn away but does not make them movable: moving, duplicating, resizing-with-an-icon, or re-wrapping a block containing one is refused outright rather than attempted. FNT-21 (planned, P6) tracks doing this by reusing the document's own Type3 glyph procedure (or the emoji's own drawn glyph) instead of redrawing it through a fallback font.

FNT-20's icon-cluster joiner handling (engine/fonts/icons.py) attaches ZWJ, variation selectors and the combining enclosing keycap (U+20E3) to a preceding icon, but not an ASCII digit before a keycap (e.g. the three codepoints of a keycap digit emoji like 1\uFE0F\u20E3) -- not seen in any real document reviewed, so left undocumented-but-untested rather than guessed at.

The standard-14 coverage check added this session (engine/fonts/resolve.py) only flags characters outside plain Latin-1 (engine.fonts.coverage's _LATIN1_MAX_CODEPOINT = 0xFF, confirmed empirically against PyMuPDF's own insert_text behavior for its 14 built-in fonts). It does not attempt to substitute a different font that DOES cover the missing characters (e.g. routing an emoji/icon through the bundled Noto/Open Sans set if one of them happens to have it) -- it only makes the existing silent loss visible. A real fix for Type3 icon/emoji glyphs specifically would mean either reusing the Type3 glyph procedures directly (documented as not implemented, FNT-15) or picking a fallback font by actual glyph coverage of needed_text, not just style/metrics.
RTL scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and vertical writing are not supported for editing; planned as FNT-18 (P8).
fit=True (FNT-10) fragments a span's texttrace into one span per character, so a second edit can no longer find that text as one span. fit defaults to False until this is fixed.
FNT-09 kerning reads only legacy 'kern' tables, not GPOS pair positioning, and no GSUB ligature substitution is attempted.
Editing a shape (EDT-09) is remove-then-redraw from get_drawings() data: blend modes, pattern/shading paints and optional-content membership are not carried over -- documented in engine/shapes.py.
Image crop (EDT-08) is refused for rotated/skewed placements; image and shape boxes in the UI skip near-full-page shapes (backgrounds) so they can't swallow clicks.
Spell-check bundles only an en_US dictionary; the ignore list is per browser (localStorage), not a shared user dictionary.
Click-to-edit (UI-02) shows an approximation of the span's font family/weight/style while typing, not the document's own embedded font loaded as a browser @font-face (documented in web/README.md).

Only Windows is tested routinely (Python 3.14 via tools/gate.py, Python 3.11 via gate.py --python .venv311/...). Linux and macOS are exercised only by ci.yml's manual workflow_dispatch matrix, which costs Actions minutes: run it once before a release.
Re-verify the iLovePDF / Nitro parity tags against the vendors' current feature pages before the first release.

Owner (2026-09-30): make local hosting user-friendly through Docker -- one-command startup (no two terminals or hand-built ?token= URL) and one-click file open (file picker/drop and upload, instead of typing a server-side path; a pasted path in quotes failed as 'does not exist'). One-click open also helps the Windows app, so it can be built earlier.

EDT-17: a font/size restyle of a word or line with more than one style run redraws the whole unit in one style (the run at the edit's anchor) when the styles genuinely can't be kept -- e.g. bold toggled on text whose own font family had to be guessed rather than read by name. This is never silent: the result names the runs affected and sets requires_approval.

EDT-17/18: reordering words or rewriting most of a mixed-style line gives the new words the style of the run at their position, not the meaning the person intended (e.g. swapping two words can make the wrong one bold).

Moving or duplicating a line/word onto another line's baseline is flagged for approval, but if approved, later plain-text extraction can merge the two lines' glyphs into one garbled line -- pre-existing extraction behaviour, not specific to EDT-16..19.
